paragraphs: In December 2024, Old Aptiv (as defined below), a public limited company formed under the laws of Jersey on May 19, 2011, completed its previously announced reorganization transaction (the "Transaction," or the "reorganization transaction"), in which Old Aptiv established a new publicly-listed Jersey parent company, Aptiv Holdings Limited ("New Aptiv"), which is resident for tax purposes in Switzerland. As a result of the Transaction, all issued and outstanding ordinary shares of Old Aptiv were exchanged on a one-for-one basis for newly issued ordinary shares of New Aptiv. Following consummation of the Transaction, holders of Old Aptiv shares became ordinary shareholders of New Aptiv, Old Aptiv became a wholly-owned subsidiary of New Aptiv and New Aptiv was renamed "Aptiv PLC." The previous publicly-listed Jersey parent company, which was an Irish tax resident, is referred to as "Old Aptiv" throughout this Annual Report on Form 10-K. New Aptiv's ordinary shares are publicly traded on the New York Stock Exchange ("NYSE") under the symbol "APTV," the same symbol under which the Old Aptiv shares were previously listed. Aptiv PLC remains a public limited company incorporated under the laws of Jersey, and continues to be subject to U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission reporting requirements.

In December 2024, following the completion of the Transaction, Old Aptiv merged with and into Aptiv Swiss Holdings Limited ("Aptiv Swiss Holdings"), a newly formed Jersey incorporated private limited company, and a direct, wholly-owned subsidiary of New Aptiv, with Aptiv Swiss Holdings surviving as a direct, wholly owned subsidiary of New Aptiv, and Old Aptiv ceasing to exist. Except as otherwise noted, all property, rights, privileges, powers and franchises of Old Aptiv vested in Aptiv Swiss Holdings, and all debts, liabilities and duties of Old Aptiv became debts, liabilities and duties of Aptiv Swiss Holdings.

In connection with the Transaction, New Aptiv assumed Old Aptiv's long-term incentive plans and its existing obligations in connection with awards granted thereunder, and Aptiv Swiss Holdings (i) entered into a supplemental indenture to each indenture in which Aptiv Swiss Holdings assumed all of Old Aptiv's obligations under each series of Old Aptiv's outstanding Notes and (ii) entered into an assumption and/or supplement agreement relating to the Credit Agreement in which New Aptiv assumed all of Old Aptiv's obligations under the Credit Agreement as the "parent entity" thereunder. In addition, New Aptiv (i) entered into a supplemental indenture to each indenture in which New Aptiv guaranteed the outstanding Notes and (ii) entered into a guarantee joinder relating to the Credit Agreement in which New Aptiv guaranteed the obligations under the Credit Agreement. Following the reorganization transaction, Aptiv Swiss Holdings (i) replaced Old Aptiv as a guarantor of the borrowers' obligations under the Credit Agreement, and (ii) succeeded to Old Aptiv as an obligor under the senior notes and the junior notes, and New Aptiv became a guarantor under the Credit Agreement (and will act as the "parent entity" thereunder) and the indentures.

As a result of the Transaction described above, there were no material changes in Aptiv PLC's operations or governance. The consolidated financial statements have been prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America ("U.S. GAAP").

References in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including the exhibits being filed as part of this report, to "Aptiv PLC," "Aptiv," the "Company," "we," "us" and "our" refers to Old Aptiv (Aptiv PLC before the Transaction in December 2024) and to New Aptiv (Aptiv PLC after the Transaction in December 2024).

On January 22, 2025, we announced our intention to pursue a separation of our Electrical Distribution Systems business into a new, independent publicly traded company, through a transaction expected to be treated as a tax-free spin-off to its shareholders (the "Separation"). The Company plans to complete the Separation by April 1, 2026, subject to customary closing conditions. The new publicly traded Electrical Distributions Systems spin-off company will be named Versigent, and will trade on the NYSE under the symbol "VGNT" following the distribution date.

During the year ended December 31, 2025, the Company incurred costs of approximately $178 million related to the Separation. These costs, which are included in selling, general and administrative expense within the consolidated statements of operations, are primarily related to third-party professional fees associated with planning the Separation. The Company expects to continue to incur additional expenses related to the Separation through the completion of the transaction.

In connection with the Separation, in the first quarter of 2025, Aptiv realigned its business into three reportable operating segments: Advanced Safety and User Experience, Engineered Components Group and Electrical Distribution Systems. Prior period amounts have been adjusted retrospectively to reflect the change in reportable operating segments, consistent with the current year presentation, throughout the audited consolidated financial statements contained herein.

Commencing with the first Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q of 2026, Aptiv will rename its Advanced Safety and User Experience segment to Intelligent Systems, and will rename its Engineered Components Group segment to Engineered Components. There is no impact to the composition of either segment.

Aptiv is a global industrial technology company focused on enabling a more automated, electrified and digitalized future. We deliver flexible and scalable solutions that support our customers' transition to an increasingly software-defined future. Our

technologies reach from sensor to cloud, including the hardware and software necessary to support automotive and other industries on a global basis. Our Advanced Safety and User Experience segment provides advanced software and services, intelligent sensors and high-performance compute platforms; our Engineered Components Group segment provides connection systems, high-performance interconnects, and cable management and protection solutions; and our Electrical Distribution Systems segment provides low voltage and high voltage power, signal and data distribution.

We are one of the largest vehicle technology suppliers and our customers include the 25 largest automotive original equipment manufacturers ("OEMs") in the world, as well as many of the leading aerospace and defense companies and global telecom operators. We operate 139 major manufacturing facilities and 11 major technical centers utilizing a regional service model that enables us to efficiently and effectively serve our global customers from best cost countries. We have a presence in 50 countries and have approximately 20,700 scientists, engineers and technicians focused on developing market relevant product solutions for our customers.

We are focused on growing and improving the profitability of our businesses, and have implemented a strategy designed to position the Company to deliver industry-leading long-term shareholder returns. This strategy includes disciplined investing in our business to grow and enhance our product offerings, strategically focusing our portfolio in high-technology, high-growth spaces in order to meet consumer preferences and leveraging an industry-leading cost structure to expand our operating margins.

Aptiv's website address is aptiv.com. Our Annual Reports on Form 10-K, Quarterly Reports on Form 10-Q, Current Reports on Form 8-K and amendments to those reports filed or furnished pursuant to Section 13(a) or 15(d) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the "Exchange Act") are available free of charge through ir.aptiv.com as soon as reasonably practicable after they are electronically filed with, or furnished to, the Securities and Exchange Commission ("SEC").

headings: Risks Related to Business Environment and Economic Conditions
Disruptions in the supply of raw materials and other supplies that we and our customers use in our products may adversely affect our profitability.
The cyclical nature of automotive sales and production can adversely affect our business.
A drop in the market share and changes in product mix offered by our customers can impact our revenues.
Our business in China is subject to aggressive competition and is sensitive to economic and market conditions.
We operate in the highly competitive automotive technology and component supply industry, and are dependent on the acceptance of new product introductions for continued growth.
If we do not respond appropriately, the evolution of the automotive industry towards autonomous vehicles and mobility on demand services could adversely affect our business.
We have invested substantial resources in markets and technologies where we expect growth and we may be unable to timely alter our strategies should such expectations not be realized.
We may not be able to respond quickly enough to changes in regulations, technology and technological risks, and to develop our intellectual property into commercially viable products.
Declines in the market share or business of our five largest customers may adversely impact our revenues and profitability.
We may not realize sales represented by awarded business.
Our inability to effectively manage the timing, quality and costs of new program launches could adversely affect our financial performance.
Adverse developments affecting one or more of our suppliers could harm our profitability.
The discontinuation or loss of business, or lack of commercial success with respect to a particular product for which we are a significant supplier could reduce our sales and harm our profitability.
Increases in costs of the materials and other supplies that we use in our products may have a negative impact on our business.

Our hedging activities to address commodity price fluctuations may not be successful in offsetting future increases in those costs or may reduce or eliminate the benefits of any decreases in those costs.
We may encounter manufacturing challenges.
Changes in factors that impact the determination of our non-U.S. pension liabilities may adversely affect us.
We may suffer future asset impairment and other restructuring charges, including write downs of long-lived assets, goodwill, or intangible assets.
Employee strikes and labor-related disruptions involving us or one or more of our customers or suppliers may adversely affect our operations.
We are exposed to foreign currency fluctuations as a result of our substantial global operations, which may affect our financial results.
We face risks associated with doing business in various national and local jurisdictions.
paragraphs: Set forth below are certain risks and uncertainties that could adversely affect our results of operations or financial condition and cause our actual results to differ materially from those expressed in forward-looking statements made by the Company. Also refer to the Cautionary Statement Regarding Forward-Looking Information in this Annual Report.

We and our customers use a broad range of materials and supplies, including copper and other metals, petroleum-based resins, chemicals, electronic components and semiconductors. A significant disruption in the supply of these materials for any reason could decrease our production and shipping levels, which could materially increase our operating costs and materially decrease our profit margins.

We, as with other component manufacturers in the automotive industry, ship products to our customers' vehicle assembly plants throughout the world so they are delivered on a "just-in-time" basis in order to maintain low inventory levels. Our suppliers also use a similar method. However, this "just-in-time" method makes the logistics supply chain in our industry very complex and very vulnerable to disruptions.

Such disruptions could be caused by any one of a myriad of potential problems, such as closures of one of our or our suppliers' plants or critical manufacturing lines due to strikes, mechanical breakdowns or failures, electrical outages, fires, explosions, political upheaval, terrorism or war, material shortages, as well as logistical complications due to weather, global climate change, volcanic eruptions, or other natural or nuclear disasters, delayed customs processing, the spread of an infectious disease, virus or other widespread illness and more. Additionally, as we focus operations in best cost countries, the risk for such disruptions is heightened. The lack of any single subcomponent necessary to manufacture one of our products could force us to cease production, potentially for a prolonged period. Similarly, a potential quality issue could force us to halt deliveries while we validate the products. Even where products are ready to be shipped, or have been shipped, delays may arise before they reach our customer. Our customers may halt or delay their production for the same reason if one of their other suppliers fails to deliver necessary components. This may cause our customers, in turn to suspend their orders, or instruct us to suspend delivery, of our products, which may adversely affect our financial performance.

When we fail to make timely deliveries in accordance with our contractual obligations, we generally have to absorb our own costs for identifying and solving the "root cause" problem as well as expeditiously producing replacement components or products. Generally, we must also carry the costs associated with "catching up," such as overtime and premium freight.

Additionally, if we are the cause for a customer being forced to halt production, the customer may seek to recoup all of its losses and expenses from us. These losses and expenses could be significant and may include consequential losses such as lost profits. Any global supply chain disruption, however small, could potentially cause the complete shutdown of an assembly line of one of our customers, and any such shutdown that is due to causes that are within our control could expose us to material claims of compensation. Where a customer halts production because of another supplier failing to deliver on time, there can be no assurance we will be fully compensated, if at all.

paragraphs: 2024年12月，Old Aptiv（以下定義），一家根據澤西法律設立的公開有限公司，於2011年5月19日成立，完成其先前公告的重組交易（"交易"或"重組交易"），其中Old Aptiv設立了一家新的公開上市的澤西母公司Aptiv Holdings Limited（"New Aptiv"），該公司就稅務目的而言設立於瑞士。根據交易，Old Aptiv所有發行在外的普通股以一對一方式交換為New Aptiv新發行的普通股。交易完成後，Old Aptiv股東成為New Apt,iv普通股股東，Old Aptiv成為New Aptiv的 wholly-owned subsidiary，且New Aptiv更名為"Aptiv PLC"。本年度10-K表報表中提及的先前公開上市的澤西母公司，為一愛爾蘭稅務居民，於本年度報表中稱為"Old Aptiv"。New Aptiv的普通股在紐約證券交易所（"NYSE"）上市交易，代碼為"APTV"，與Old Aptiv股權原先上市的代碼相同。Aptiv PLC仍為根據澤西法律設立的公開有限公司，並持續受美國證券交易委員會（SEC）的報告要求所規範。

2024年12月，交易完成後，Old Aptiv與Aptiv Swiss Holdings Limited（"Aptiv Swiss Holdings"）合併，Aptiv Swiss Holdings為一新設立的澤西註冊私人有限公司，為New Aptiv的直接 wholly-owned subsidiary，且Aptiv Swiss Holdings為New Aptiv的直接 wholly-owned subsidiary，Old Aptiv則停止存在。除非另有說明，Old Aptiv的所有財產、權利、特權、權力及特許權均轉移至Aptiv Swiss Holdings，且Old Aptiv的所有債務、負債及義務均成為Aptiv Swiss Holdings的債務、負債及義務。

根據交易，New Aptiv承繼Old Aptiv的長期激勵計畫及其現有義務，與根據該計畫所授予的獎勵有關。此外，Aptiv Swiss Holdings（i）與每一份Indenture簽訂補充契約，並承繼Old Aptiv根據每一系列 Outstanding Notes 所負的義務；（ii）與Credit Agreement簽訂擔保及補充契約，New Aptiv承繼Old Aptiv根據Credit Agreement所負的義務，作為該契約下的"parent entity"。此外，New Aptiv（i）與每一份Indenture簽訂補充契約，擔保Outstanding Notes；（ii）與Credit Agreement簽訂擔保加入契約，New Aptiv擔保Credit Agreement下的義務。重組交易後，Aptiv Swiss Holdings（i）取代Old Aptiv成為借款人義務的擔保人；（ii）繼承Old Aptiv作為高階債券及低階債券的義務人，New Aptiv成為Credit Agreement下的擔保人（並作為該契約下的"parent entity"）及Indentures。
根據上述交易，Aptiv PLC的營運或治理未有重大變動。合併財務報表已根據美國通用會計準則（"U.S. GAAP"）編製。
本年度10-K表報表中，包括作為本報告一部分所提交的附屬文件，提及"Aptiv PLC"、"Aptiv"、"本公司"、"我們"、"我們"及"我們"，均指Old Aptiv（交易前的Aptiv PLC）及New Aptiv（交易後的Aptiv PLC）。
2025年1月22日，本公司宣佈有意將電氣配電系統業務分拆為一家新的、獨立上市的公司，透過一項預期被視為稅務無負擔的分拆交易（"分拆"）。本公司預計於2026年4月1日完成分拆，視乎常規交易條件。新上市的電氣配電系統分拆公司將名為Versigent，並於分拆後在紐約證券交易所（NYSE）以代碼"VGNT"交易。
在2025年12月31日結業年度，本公司因分拆產生約1.78億美元的費用。這些費用已包含於合併營運費用中，主要與規劃分拆的第三方專業費用有關。本公司預計在交易完成前，仍會產生額外與分拆相關的費用。
根據分拆，於2025年第一季，Aptiv將其業務重新調整為三個應報告營運分部：先進安全與用戶體驗、工程零組件集團及電氣配電系統。過往期間的金額已回溯調整，以反映應報告營運分部的變動，與當前年份的呈現方式一致，並包含於本報告中審計的合併財務報表中。
自2026年第一季財務報告（Form 10-Q）起，Aptiv將其Advanced Safety and User Experience應報告分部更名為Intelligent Systems，並將其Engineered Components Group應報告分部更名為Engineered Components。此更名不會影響任一應報告分部的組成。
Aptiv為一間全球工業科技公司，專注於協助實現更自動化、電動化與數位化的未來。我們提供靈活且可擴展的解決方案，協助客戶轉型至日益軟體定義的未來。我們的

技術範疇從感測器延伸至雲端，包括支援汽車及其他產業在全球範圍內所需的硬體與軟體。我們的Advanced Safety and User Experience應報告分部提供先進軟體與服務、智慧感測器與高性能計算平台；我們的Engineered Components Group應報告分部提供連接系統、高性能連接器與電纜管理與保護解決方案；而我們的Electrical Distribution Systems應報告分部提供低壓與高壓電力、訊號與數據分配解決方案。
我們是全球最大車用科技供應商之一，客戶包括全球25大汽車原廠（"OEMs"），以及許多領先的航空與防禦公司與全球電信業者。我們擁有139個主要製造廠與11個主要技術中心，採用區域服務模式，使我們能從最佳成本國家有效且高效地服務全球客戶。我們在50個國家設有據點，約有20,700位科學家、工程師與技術人員專注於為客戶開發符合市場需求的產品解決方案。
我們專注於成長與提升各業務的獲利能力，並已實施一項策略，以使本公司能提供產業領先的長期股東回報。此策略包括對業務進行審慎投資，以成長與提升產品組合，戰略性地聚焦於高科技、高成長領域，以符合消費者偏好，並利用產業領先的成本結構來擴大營運毛利。
Aptiv的網站網址為aptiv.com。本公司依照證券交易法1934年（"Exchange Act"）第13(a)或15(d)條項所提交的年度報告（Form 10-K）、季報（Form 10-Q）、現況報告（Form 8-K）以及這些報告的更正文件，均可免費於ir.aptiv.com網站上取得，自這些文件電子提交至，或提供至美國證券交易委員會（"SEC"）後即時提供。

paragraphs: Aptiv 為一全球性工業科技公司，專注於實現更自動化、電動化與數位化的未來。我們提供靈活且可擴展的解決方案，協助客戶轉型至日益軟體定義的未來。我們的技術從感測器延伸至雲端，包括支援汽車及其他產業全球運作所需的硬體與軟體。我們的先進安全與用戶體驗分部提供先進軟體與服務、智慧感測器與高性能計算平台；我們的工程零組件集團分部提供連接系統、高性能連接器與線纜管理與保護解決方案；而我們的電氣配電系統分部則提供低壓與高壓電力、訊號與數據配電。
我們是全球最大車輛科技供應商之一，客戶包括全球前 25 大汽車原廠製造商（"OEMs"），以及許多領先的航空與防禦公司與全球電信業者。

2024 年 12 月，Old Aptiv（如下所定義）完成其先前公告的重組交易（"Transaction" 或 "重組交易"），其中 Old Aptiv 成立了一家新的公開上市的澤西母公司 Aptiv Holdings Limited（"New Aptiv"），該公司就稅務目的而言設立於瑞士。根據該交易，Old Aptiv 所有發行及流通的普通股以一對一的比例交換為新發行的 New Aptiv 普通股。交易完成後，Old Aptiv 股東成為 New Aptiv 的普通股股東，Old Aptiv 成為 New Aptiv 的 wholly-owned 子公司，且 New Aptiv 更名為 "Aptiv PLC"。先前公開上市的澤西母公司，其稅務居民為愛爾蘭，於本年度報告 10-K 中稱為 "Old Aptiv"。New Aptiv 的普通股在紐約證券交易所（"NYSE"）上市交易，代號為 "APTV"，與 Old Aptiv 股票先前上市的代號相同。Aptiv PLC 繼續為根據澤西法律設立的公開有限公司，並持續受美國證券交易委員會的報告要求所規範。

2024 年 12 月，交易完成後，Old Aptiv 合併進 Aptiv Swiss Holdings Limited（"Aptiv Swiss Holdings"），一家新成立的澤西註冊私人有限公司，為 New Aptiv 的直接、 wholly-owned 子公司，且 Aptiv Swiss Holdings 繼續作為 New Aptiv 的直接、 wholly-owned 子公司，Old Aptiv 則停止存在。除非另有說明，Old Aptiv 的所有財產、權利、特權、權力與特許權均轉移至 Aptiv Swiss Holdings，且 Old Aptiv 的所有債務、負債與義務均成為 Aptiv Swiss Holdings 的債務、負債與義務。根據上述交易，Aptiv PLC 的運作或治理並未出現重大變更。

根據該交易，New Aptiv 承接 Old Aptiv 的長期激勵計畫及其現有義務，與根據該計畫所授予的獎勵有關。此外，Aptiv Swiss Holdings（i）與每一份 indenture 簽訂補充契約，使其承擔 Old Aptiv 在每一系列 Outstanding Notes 下的所有義務；（ii）與 Credit Agreement 簽訂擔保與/或補充協議，使 New Aptiv 承擔 Credit Agreement 下 Old Aptiv 的所有義務，作為該協議下的 "parent entity"。此外，New Aptiv（i）與每一份 indenture 簽訂補充契約，使其擔保 Outstanding Notes；（ii）與 Credit Agreement 簽訂擔保加入協議，使 New Aptiv 擔保 Credit Agreement 下的義務。交易完成後，Aptiv Swiss Holdings（i）取代 Old Aptiv 作為 Credit Agreement 下借款人義務的擔保人；（ii）繼承 Old Aptiv 作為高階債券與低階債券的義務人，且 New Aptiv 成為 Credit Agreement 下的擔保人（並將作為該協議下的 "parent entity"），並擔保 indentures。

headings: 與商業環境及經濟條件相關的風險
我們與客戶在產品中使用的原材料及其他供應品之供應中斷，可能對我們的獲利造成不利影響。
汽車銷售與生產的週期性特質可能對我們的業務造成不利影響。
客戶市場佔有率下降及產品組合變動，可能影響我們的營業收入。
我們在中國的業務面臨強烈競爭，且對經濟與市場條件變化相當敏感。
我們營運於高度競爭的汽車科技與零組件供應產業，並依賴新產品的接受度以維持持續成長。
若我們未能適當回應，汽車產業朝向自動駕駛車與隨需應變運輸服務的演進，可能對我們的業務造成不利影響。
我們已於預期成長的市場與技術上投入大量資源，若相關預期未實現，我們可能無法及時調整策略。
我們可能無法迅速回應規範、技術及技術風險的變化，並將我們的智慧財產權發展為具商業價值的產品。
我們五大客戶的市佔率或業務下降，可能對我們的營業收入及獲利產生不利影響。
我們可能無法實現已獲取業務所代表的銷售額。
我們若無法有效管理新產品上市的時程、品質及成本，可能對我們的財務表現產生不利影響。
影響我們一個或數個供應商的不利情況，可能損害我們的獲利能力。
我們若是重要供應商，且某項產品的業務中斷或失去商業成功，可能減少我們的銷售額並損害我們的獲利能力。
我們產品所使用的材料及其他供應品的成本增加，可能對我們的業務產生負面影響。
我們為應對原物料價格波動而進行的避險活動，可能無法成功抵消未來成本的增加，或可能減少或消除任何成本下降所帶來的效益。
我們可能面臨製造方面的挑戰。
影響我們非美國退休金負債認定的因素變動，可能對我們造成不利影響。
我們可能未來遭遇資產減損及其他重整費用，包括長期資產、商譽或無形資產的減記。
我們或我們的客戶、供應商發生員工罷工及勞動相關的中斷，可能對我們的營運造成不利影響。
由於我們龐大的全球營運，我們面臨外幣波動的風險，這可能影響我們的財務結果。
我們在各個國家及地方司法管轄區從事業務時，面臨相關風險。
paragraphs: 下列為可能對本公司營運成果或財務狀況產生不利影響，並導致實際結果與本公司所作之預測性陳述有重大差異之風險與不確定性。另請參閱本年度報告中之預測性資訊警示聲明。
本公司與客戶使用廣泛之材料與供應品，包括銅與其他金屬、石油基樹脂、化學品、電子零組件與半導體。若因任何原因導致這些材料之供應出現重大中斷，將可能降低本公司之生產與出貨量，進而大幅提高營運成本，並大幅降低毛利率。
本公司，如同汽車產業其他零組件製造商，將產品運送到客戶之車輛組裝廠，以「即時到貨」方式交付，以維持低存貨水準。供應商亦採用類似方式。然而，此「即時到貨」方式使本產業之供應鏈物流變得非常複雜，且極易受到中斷影響。

此類中斷可能由多種潛在問題所導致，例如本公司或供應商之一個廠區或關鍵製造線因罷工、機械故障或失敗、電力中斷、火災、爆炸、政治動盪、恐怖主義或戰爭、材料短缺，以及因天氣、全球氣候變遷、火山爆發或其他自然或核災害所導致之物流問題，或因傳染病、病毒或其他廣泛疾病所導致之延遲。此外，因本公司將營運集中於成本最佳化國家，此類中斷之風險亦相對提高。若缺乏任何單一子零組件以製造本公司之一項產品，將可能導致本公司停止生產，且可能持續一段時間。同樣地，潛在之品質問題可能導致本公司停止出貨，直到產品經驗證為止。即使產品已準備好出貨，或已出貨，也可能在到達客戶前出現延遲。若客戶之其他供應商未能如期交付必要零組件，其客戶可能也會停止或延遲生產。此可能導致客戶暫停訂單，或指示本公司暫停交付產品，進而對本公司之財務表現造成不利影響。
若本公司未能依約定時間交付，通常需自行承擔識別並解決「根本原因」問題之成本，以及迅速生產替代零組件或產品之成本。通常，本公司亦需承擔「追趕」所產生之成本，例如加班與高價運費。

此外，若本公司是導致客戶被迫停止生產之原因，客戶可能要求本公司賠償其所有損失與費用。這些損失與費用可能相當重大，且可能包括間接損失，例如損失之利潤。然而，任何全球供應鏈之中斷，即使規模極小，也可能導致本公司客戶之一個組裝線完全停擺，而任何因本公司控制範圍內之原因所導致之停擺，可能使本公司面臨重大賠償請求。若客戶因其他供應商未能如期交付而停止生產，本公司無法保證是否能獲得全部賠償，甚至可能無法獲得賠償。
